  \caption{Heart-100: signals (rows) by seed (columns). A seed carries a signal when its logit contribution has a standard deviation of at least 0.10 logit over the training patients, after clipping to the 1st--99th percentiles; w: weak (0.03 to 0.10), not counted. Linear core: the contribution is the term's weight times the input, the weight from the least-squares projection of the seed's logit on the linear terms (zero when the seed does not read the input); \checkmark{} in the direction most seeds give it (the row's words), opp: the opposite. Notes: networks with a purely linear path for the input; the range of the contribution SD. Non-linear units, by the inputs that switch them: the contribution is the change in the logit when the family's units are replaced by their straight-line fit; per seed, the number of units and whether being on raises ($+$) or lowers ($-$) risk against that fit ($\pm$: both). Notes: \emph{recurring}, another seed reproduces its non-linear residual; \emph{near-linear}, too close to linear to match.}
  \label{tab:exp2-signals-heart100}
